body: Solera Multifamily, LLC and Hickory Investors, LLC allege they invested almost $3 million in Old Hickory Village, a 2022 real estate development in St. Peters, Missouri, and that Jeffrey J. Tegethoff and the development companies he owns used the money for other purposes, Missouri Lawyers Media reported. The plaintiffs say contractors were not paid on time, the project was delayed, and other investors had to make additional capital contributions that diluted their shares, and that a request to review the books was ignored. The suit, filed December 26, 2025 in the Eastern District of Missouri (No. 4:25-CV-1877-JMB), asserted breach of contract, breach of fiduciary duty, fraud in the inducement, state and federal securities fraud, theft and conversion, unjust enrichment and declaratory relief.

The defendants moved to dismiss, arguing the fraud allegations lacked particularity. The plaintiffs did not respond to the motion and instead sought leave to file an amended complaint that dropped the federal securities claim; the defendants argued the change was meant to avoid federal limits on discovery. In a June 17, 2026 order, Judge Bodenhausen noted that the plaintiffs had 'wholly failed to respond' to the dismissal arguments but granted leave to amend under Rule 15's generous standard, denied the motion to dismiss without prejudice to refiling as to the non-bankrupt defendants, and stayed the case as to Tegethoff Development, LLC and Tegethoff Development Co, LLC, which had filed for Chapter 11.

On September 22, 2026, the court stayed the whole case. The order notes that the automatic bankruptcy stay does not apply to non-bankrupt defendants, but finds it efficient to pause the case given the intertwined claims, denies a renewed motion to dismiss and a motion to stay discovery without prejudice, and requires status reports on the bankruptcy starting December 18, 2026. Lawyers for both sides did not respond to Missouri Lawyers Media's requests for comment.

timeline.label: Solera Multifamily and Hickory Investors sue Jeffrey Tegethoff, his development companies and two related trusts
Defendants move to dismiss parts of the amended complaint
Judge Bodenhausen grants leave to amend, denies the motion to dismiss without prejudice, and stays claims against the two bankrupt Tegethoff Development entities
Court stays the entire case pending the bankruptcy and orders status reports beginning December 18, 2026
